result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend stacking, cropping and avoiding improvement claims. A does it more tightly: a 3×2 grid of the six steps over one full-width page, three markers that each map back to the old steps, and a clear list of what to cut. B suggests similar things but drifts into extras like mobile wrapping, reserving image space and a result placeholder, and it adds more pins, some of them judgments ('competes with the form') rather than visible changes. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers stack the images within the 720px column, crop away the full-height screenshots and avoid claiming any improvement. B is tighter: its 3×2 grid shows six pages against one, it limits annotations to the promo callout and three markers showing which old steps each part of the new page replaced, and its leave-out list is sharper (sliders, legible tile detail). A adds side points that pull focus from the comparison, such as reserving figure box sizes and when to break out wider.
